title: Spontaneous optical emission of a randomly oriented chiral quantum source
abstract: We derive the form of the one-photon state of the electromagnetic field resulting from spontaneous optical emission of a randomly oriented chiral quantum source, including electric dipole, magnetic dipole, and electric quadrupole contributions to the radiation. We describe how spatial coherence in the emission can be exploited to reveal hidden information about the emitter. This work serves as a prelude and companion piece to our concurrently submitted work \cite{Backlund2026Letter} in which we present the classical and quantum error bounds associated with assigning the handedness of such an emitter.
summary: This theoretical paper derives the quantum state of light emitted from randomly oriented chiral sources, accounting for electric dipole, magnetic dipole, and quadrupole contributions. It shows that measuring correlations between photons collected in different directions or polarizations allows experimental separation of these underlying physical coupling parameters. This advances understanding of symmetry breaking in spontaneous emission.
main_problem: The paper derives the quantum state of light emitted via spontaneous optical emission from a randomly oriented chiral source, aiming to characterize the multipolar nature ($\mu, m, Q$) of this emission.
main_result: By analyzing spatial coherence and collecting photons in specific polarization/direction combinations (e.g., opposite directions), one can isolate parameters related to electric dipole, magnetic dipole, and quadrupole moments.
method: The analysis uses quantum electrodynamics formalism, deriving density matrices ($ ar{ho}$) for the emitted photon state by averaging over random source orientations and projecting onto specific polarization/propagation modes.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum emitter (modeled as a two-level system) undergoing spontaneous emission into the electromagnetic field. The interaction Hamiltonian includes electric dipole, magnetic dipole, and electric quadrupole terms.
key_observables: The one-photon state density operator ($ ar{ho}$), which depends on polarization basis states (L/R circular polarization) and collection directions ($\hat{z}, \hat{x}$).
important_parameters: Unitless parameters $\epsilon_\mu, \epsilon_m, \epsilon_Q$ characterizing the relative strengths of dipole, magnetic dipole, and quadrupole contributions.
main_assumptions: The emitter is treated as a two-level system; rotational averaging is performed over all source orientations; approximations are made in the continuum limit for quadrupole terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate collection geometries using polarizers and apertures, showing how measurements can be restricted to specific polarization/direction combinations (e.g., opposite $\hat{z}$ propagation).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the general one-photon state ($ho$) including all multipoles, simplifying this for random orientation averages, and finally developing measurement protocols using circular polarizations and directional correlations to separate the underlying physical parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantum optical framework for characterizing chiral emitters by exploiting spatial coherence, which is crucial for understanding fundamental symmetries in light-matter interactions beyond simple dipole approximations.
